Cobalt Superconformal Electrodeposition

and Wenquan Lv<sup>2,z</sup>
<sup>1</sup>State Key Laboratory ofUrban Water Resource and Environment, School ofChemistry and Chemical Engineering, Harbin

Cyclic voltammetry (CV), chronopotentiometry and quartz crystal microbalance were used to study the effect of Malachite Green
(MG) on bottom-up growth of cobalt. The addition of MG not only inhibited the reduction of
\mathrm { C o } ^ { 2 + }
but also accelerated the
hydrogen evolution process. The metal reduction process was enhanced as well as the current efficiency was higher with the
increase of pH. The bottom-up growth of cobalt can be achieved with the potential of −1.20 V. Induction-diffusion-adsorption
superconformal electrodeposition mechanism was proposed to illustrate the synergistic effect of MG and pH on the growth of
cobalt. On one hand, the MG concentration gradient and pH gradient could be formed to achieve a growth rate difference within
blind vias so as to obtain bottom-up growth (diffusion-adsorption effect). On the other hand, the growth rate difference was
intensified due to the accelerating effect of MG on HER so as to boost the cobalt superfilling (induction effect).

Since the copper plating process, namely Damascus Copper
Plating process, has been proposed by IBM in order to achieve metal
interconnect integrated circuits (IC), it has attracted a great deal of
attention in terms of electroplating technology in electronic devices
with metal deposition of copper interconnect line.<sup>1</sup> Up to now, the
damascene plating technology is still leading technology for the
production of large scale integration (LSI) devices.
However, within the manufacturing process of back-end-of-line
(BEOL), the width of interconnect lines has been downscaled to
nano level with the density of LSI devices becoming more and more
compressed according to the Moore’s Law. Resulting in the increase
of the copper resistivity and RC delay, which has become the key
factors for restricting the performance of the integration devices.<sup>2,3</sup>
For example, the resistivity of a 10 nm-wide Cu interconnect line is
more than ten times higher than that of bulk copper due to the severe
electrons scattering and grain boundaries scattering.<sup>4,5</sup>
As a result, it is of great importance to screen metals with low
electron mean free path in the replacement of Cu in order to improve
the property of IC. Among these metals with relatively low mean
free path, Co was investigated widely as interconnect line after
balancing the production cost and IC property.<sup>6–11</sup> Since cobalt not
only is of low fine-line resistivity, but also is of strong electro-
migration resistance.<sup>12,13</sup>
Applying electrodeposition method to prepare Co thin films is a
cost-friendly, fast, and easy-operating method, and has been applied
in many fields.<sup>14–17</sup> Achieving bottom-up growth of cobalt is the key
to manufacturing the interconnect line, while the superconformal
electrodeposition of cobalt can be obtained by exploring additive,<sup>18</sup>
and optimizing the electrodeposition parameters, including the
composition of bath solution,<sup>19</sup> current density,<sup>20</sup> pH<sup>21</sup> and so on.
Besides, Co film with different structure and crystal phase can be
obtained by changing electrodeposition parameters.<sup>22</sup> Generally, the
Watts-based electrolyte or buffered sulfate electrolyte can be used to
deposit Co film, in which boric acid has been added to stabilize the
increasing pH in plating bath caused by polyborates and primarily
triborate and occupy block surface sites to inhibit HER as well as
facilitate cobalt deposition by the surface complex with cobalt.<sup>23–25</sup>
In order to achieve bottom-up growth of cobalt deposit, appropriate
additives should be introduced into plating bath to achieve growth
rate difference in the blind vias.<sup>26–28</sup>
And, this difference is
consistent with the diffusion-adsorption mechanism.<sup>29–32</sup>
Josell et al.<sup>28</sup> realized the superconformation filling of TSVs with
high aspect ratio by adding polyethyleneimine (PEI) as suppressor
into the plating solution, which is composed of cobalt sulfate, cobalt
chloride and boric acid. The deposition mechanism is due to the
occurrence of S-NDR characteristics after the breakdown of the
adsorption of PEI on the cathode surface, in which active-passive
transitions are formed in TSVs with the applied voltage. Hydrogen
induction deactivation mechanism was proposed to explain the
influence of additive XF on superfilling of cobalt by Wu et al.<sup>33</sup>
The growth rate different within blind vias was ascribed to the fact
that the deactivation rate of additive is higher than the compensatory
rate by mass transport. Huang et al.<sup>34</sup> added the dioxime additive as
suppressor to achieve Co defect-free filling. Co(DMG) complex can
be formed between dioxime and cobalt ions so as to inhibit the Co
reduction. When the voltage rises to the breakdown threshold, Co
begins to deposit on the cathode surface. Under the influence of
convection, an obvious inhibition gradient was formed during the
deposition process, which is consistent with S-NDR mechanism.
In this study, Malachite Green (MG), was selected as a
suppressor for cobalt electrodeposition. It has been verified that
MG adsorbed on the cathode surface to inhibit the reduction of
copper and titanium.<sup>35</sup> And the influence of MG on Co metal
deposition process have also been discussed before,<sup>36</sup> so this paper
mainly studies the influence of MG adsorption on the hydrogen
evolution process. The electrochemical tests, including cyclic
voltammetry (CV) and linear sweeping voltammetry (LSV), were
applied to research the inhibition ability of MG on the deposition
process of cobalt, while the influence of MG on HER was also
studied by EQCM tests. Superconformal electrodeposition of cobalt
was achieved and induction-diffusion-adsorption mechanism was
proposed to illustrate the synergistic effect of MG and pH.
